source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Replace root-cause analysis because a dashboard alone identifies every underlying cause and corrective action.","B":"Hide unit-level measures until the end of the year, because frequent performance visibility can bias improvement efforts.","C":"Display only favorable measures, because incomplete positive data are more useful for staff engagement than balanced trends.","D":"Give staff timely visibility into selected quality measures, trends, and gaps so improvement work can be monitored."}}
source_row.rationale: A quality dashboard makes defined performance measures and trends visible to the care team, supporting monitoring and feedback; it complements rather than replaces valid measurement and root-cause/improvement analysis.
source_row.source_detail: Quality-improvement guidance describes using measures over time to monitor progress, make performance visible and determine whether interventions are associated with improvement; dashboards are a presentation mechanism, not a substitute for analysis. AHRQ CAHPS Improvement Guide page last reviewed March 2026; rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: AHRQ — Monitoring Progress with Quality Measures
source_row.stem: A unit displays an accessible dashboard of current fall, infection and hand-hygiene metrics. What is the main quality-improvement benefit?
